devops.interview_framing: How does eBPF kernel tracing eliminate sidecar proxy CPU overhead in high-throughput Kubernetes clusters?

flashcards.question: How does eBPF-based observability differ from traditional sidecar proxy telemetry (e.g., Envoy)?
flashcards.answer: eBPF runs bytecode directly inside the Linux kernel, capturing socket and network metrics across all pods on a node with <1% CPU overhead, eliminating sidecar memory bloat and context-switch latency.

Title: Kernel-Level Observability with eBPF and OpenTelemetry
Source: eBPF Foundation & CNCF (2026)

Section 1: The Overhead of Sidecar Proxies.
Injecting Envoy sidecars into thousands of microservice pods consumes gigabytes of memory and adds 2-5ms hop latency. eBPF hooks into kernel socket buffers directly, observing all TCP handshakes with near-zero overhead.
